paragraphs: The GLS450 has been part of the GLS range since 2016, spanning two generations under the same badge. The earlier X166 generation (2016–2019) uses the M276 — a 3.0-litre V6 petrol engine with mild hybrid assistance introduced during the GLS's early years. From 2019, the X167-generation GLS450 switched to the M256, a newer 3.0-litre inline-six petrol mild hybrid that's a different unit entirely, not an evolution of the M276. Knowing which one your car has matters, because the components and the rebuild specifics differ between them — which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every GLS450 on the road.

cards.body: A 3.0-litre V6 petrol engine fitted to the GLS450 from 2016 to 2019. No specific known issue confirmed for this application. We replace timing chains, bearings and gaskets as standard on every rebuild.

The current 3.0-litre inline-six petrol mild hybrid engine, fitted from 2019 onwards. A genuinely different design from the M276, with its own specification. No specific known issue confirmed for this application.

compatibility.intro: Because the GLS450 spans two distinct engines across two generations, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an M276 part will work on an M256 car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (M256) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic GLS quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
